lines.text: At National Vision, owner of America's Best, eye exams brought in $254.7M in fiscal 2025. Eyeglasses and sunglasses brought in $1.27B.
lines.say: At National Vision, the company behind America's Best, eye exams brought in two hundred fifty-four point seven million dollars in fiscal twenty twenty-five. Eyeglasses and sunglasses brought in one point two seven billion.

lines.text: Divide one by the other: about $5 of glasses for every $1 of exams.
lines.say: Divide one by the other, and that's about five dollars of glasses for every dollar of exams.

lines.text: Exams were just 12.8% of its $1.99B in revenue.
lines.say: Exams were just twelve point eight percent of its one point nine nine billion dollars in revenue.

lines.text: The glasses money goes all the way up: Ray-Ban and LensCrafters owner EssilorLuxottica had €28.5B in revenue in 2025.
lines.say: And the glasses money goes all the way up. EssilorLuxottica, which owns Ray-Ban and LensCrafters, had twenty-eight point five billion euros in revenue in twenty twenty-five.

post.title: Why glasses, not eye exams, pay the eye care bills
post.ig:
Eye exams aren't the real money. Glasses are, 5 to 1.
National Vision (America's Best) took in $254.7M from eye exams in fiscal 2025, versus $1.27B from eyeglasses and sunglasses.
Exams were just 12.8% of its $1.99B revenue.
As of Dec 2024, 1,478 of its 2,393 optometrists worked for separate professional corporations.
Under the FTC Eyeglass Rule, eye doctors must give patients a free copy of their prescription right after the exam.
Sources: National Vision FY2025 and FY2024 Form 10-K, EssilorLuxottica FY2025 results, FTC.
